question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-9 & 2 & -3 \\ -3 & -8 & 12 \\ 7 & -2 & -9\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & -12 \\ -31 & 0 & 48 \\ 7 & -2 & -9\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above $a_{32}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-9 & 2 & -3 \\ -3 & -8 & 12 \\ 7 & -2 & -9\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}+R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & -12 \\ -3 & -8 & 12 \\ 7 & -2 & -9\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}-4R_{3}}\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & -12 \\ -31 & 0 & 48 \\ 7 & -2 & -9\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}+R_{3}$ and $R_{2}:=R_{2}-4R_{3}$.
